boundary: Typed presentation and official AG-UI transport only. Execution checks actual managed model and canonical ownership in the live browser; critical checks adverse events and actual same-identity replay/auth denial. Controlled owner ports test disclosure guards, not canonical persistence. Command mediation, native examiners, cyclic verification and overall A1 acceptance remain separate open requirements.

review.perspective: Challenge the delivered presentation as a hostile transport rather than repeat normal delivery: reject scope/hash/version/order substitutions, SDK callback exception loss, abort races and advisory tool/interrupt claims. Independently replay the actual production identity and reject conflicting or unauthenticated reads. Audit architecture with deliberately injected raw protocol dependencies.

findings.finding: The old terminal encoder was shared by empty-project intake, so replacing its public export with a Project-only function broke the intake boundary.
findings.resolution: Dispatch the registered intake turn through its existing generic encoder; Project-only disclosure and owner reads apply only to copilot-turn. Keep the separate intake regression.

findings.finding: The pinned SDK catches subscriber exceptions, allowing a validation throw to disappear before a collected result is returned.
findings.resolution: Record subscriber validation failure explicitly, stop propagation, and reject the result after SDK completion; a controlled official-client attack verifies this behavior.

findings.finding: An abort during an asynchronous owner read could race with disclosure, while SDK RUN_ERROR could overwrite a genuine canonical failure with disconnection.
findings.resolution: Recheck abort after each owner read and preserve failed/cancelled only when the exact retained terminal and matching error code are validated; independent adverse checks exercise both cases.

findings.finding: Feature components interpreted activity and terminal protocol strings directly.
findings.resolution: Move protocol interpretation and exact interrupt metadata parsing into adapter presentation modules; keep business type/function exports and existing feature regression tests. Core records retain their registered protocol metadata validation without importing the SDK.

findings.finding: The transient presentation store keyed only by Project could expose an earlier actor answer after a browser session changed.
findings.resolution: Use the exact authenticated token scope as part of the private store key; the component requests only its current browser session. Separate foreign-session reads cannot retrieve the previous presentation.
